quote.text: For some reason, there is this façade that life should be full of happiness and without its suffering. Which, actually makes us suffer even more. Because when we get sad or something bad happens, we do not only feel bad about the thing itself but we also feel bad because our life is not the way it is supposed to be. Not realizing suffering and sadness is just a part of life and they are inevitable.
quote.author: Cave Man
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Recognize that both joy and sorrow are natural parts of life; just as our children learn from experiencing challenges, accepting melancholy as a necessary counterbalance to happiness helps foster resilience.
    • Embrace imperfection in family life—allowing emotions to be felt without judgment teaches our children the wisdom of facing life’s inevitable difficulties with calm acceptance.
  • Leadership
    • Understand that suffering is not a flaw but a facet of human existence; a true leader acknowledges this reality and guides others by remaining calm amid adversity.
    • Instead of attempting to conceal hardships, use them as opportunities to inspire team growth and solidarity; embracing real challenges cultivates authentic respect and trust.
  • Product Management
    • In product development, setbacks and failures are inevitable; by accepting that no journey is devoid of challenges, we can focus on iterative improvement rather than the illusion of constant perfection.
    • Cultivate a mindset where each failure or disappointing outcome is seen as a valuable lesson, reinforcing that the path to success requires both recognition of pain and the resolve to overcome it.
